# torch_vn_algebra

> Python library (PyTorch, CPU and CUDA GPU) for batched computation with block-diagonal matrices in symmetry sectors, i.e. finite-dimensional Type I von Neumann algebras M = ⊕_c M_{k_c}(C). Operators are tensors of shape (batch, C, k_max, k_max). Covers random operators and Haar-random unitaries, density matrices and entropies, quantum channels (Kraus, Choi, Stinespring) within and between sectors, tensor products with charge fusion and partial traces, Schrödinger and Lindblad dynamics, spin chains in U(1), momentum and SU(2) sectors (Lanczos, Krylov), numerical Wedderburn decomposition and commutants of matrix algebras and group representations, Clebsch–Gordan coefficients, inclusions of algebras with conditional expectations and Jones indices, Jordan algebras, Petz and sandwiched Rényi divergences, and constrained batched optimisation; differentiable with autograd. MIT license. Companion paper: arXiv:2606.15882.

Install: `pip install torch_vn_algebra` (install PyTorch first). Import: `from torch_vn_algebra import TypeIAlgebra`. Python 3.9 or newer, torch >= 2.0, numpy.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/andre-a-no/von_neumann_type_i/blob/main/README.md): features, quick start, module table, comparison with QuTiP, QuSpin, Qiskit, escnn and others, limitations
- [Documentation website](https://andre-a-no.github.io/von_neumann_type_i/): lecture notes, tutorial and API reference
- [Tutorial](https://github.com/andre-a-no/von_neumann_type_i/blob/main/man/tutorial/README.md): the library chapter by chapter, every code block executed by the test suite
- [Lecture notes](https://github.com/andre-a-no/von_neumann_type_i/blob/main/man/lecture_notes/README.md): self-contained theory of finite-dimensional von Neumann algebras with complete proofs (English, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, Russian)
- [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15882): design, validation against exact results, benchmarks

## Modules

- `torch_vn_algebra.algebra`: `TypeIAlgebra` and its `Operator` (lazy, batched, functional calculus, traces, norms, random operators, Haar unitaries)
- `torch_vn_algebra.states`: `DensityMatrix`, random states, Gibbs states, entropy, relative entropy, fidelity, trace distance
- `torch_vn_algebra.channels`: `Channel` (Kraus, Choi, superoperator), `InterSectorChannel`, standard and random channels
- `torch_vn_algebra.composite`: tensor products, fused tensor products (charge conservation), partial trace
- `torch_vn_algebra.dynamics`: Schrödinger, von Neumann and Lindblad equations, propagators, Lindblad channels
- `torch_vn_algebra.chains`, `torch_vn_algebra.krylov`, `torch_vn_algebra.su2`: spin-1/2 chains in U(1), momentum and SU(2) sectors, Lanczos and Krylov methods
- `torch_vn_algebra.decompose`: Wedderburn decomposition of the algebra generated by matrices or a finite group, commutant bases, twirls
- `torch_vn_algebra.inclusions`: inclusions N ⊂ M, conditional expectations, Jones, Watatani and Pimsner–Popa indices, basic construction
- `torch_vn_algebra.divergences`: Petz and sandwiched Rényi divergences, recovery maps, noncommutative L^p norms
- `torch_vn_algebra.jordan`: Jordan products, quadratic representation, Jordan algebras generated by matrices, spin factors
- `torch_vn_algebra.optimize`: constrained parametrisations of unitaries and positive operators, batched multistart optimisation
- `torch_vn_algebra.functional`, `torch_vn_algebra.cost`: functional calculus with spectral gradients; run-time and memory safeguards
